preamble: Raising of /æ/ all the way to a high front vowel is rare and in the clearest case morphophonological. In Uyghur vowel reduction, the low unrounded vowels /ɑ æ/ raise to [i] (transcribed /ɪ/ on Wikipedia) in non-final open syllables created by suffixation (mewæ 'fruit' > mewi-si 'its fruit'). Long vowels, some loanwords and some underived stems resist the rule (hɑwɑ-si 'its weather', not *hɑwi-si). No comparable direct æ > i change is documented elsewhere.

examples.note: Stem-final /æ/ ends up in a word-medial open syllable after suffixation and raises to [i].
The same verb stem keeps /æ/ before the consonant-initial gerund suffix (closed syllable) but raises it before -di.
The medial /æ/ of the stem raises to [i]; the suffix still harmonizes to the front value of the original /æ/, an opacity effect.

sources: Mayer, C., McCollum, A., & Eziz, G. (2022). Issues in Uyghur phonology. Language and Linguistics Compass 16(12), e12478. https://doi.org/10.1111/lnc3.12478

Mayer, C. (2023). Opacity in parallel models of phonology: Insights from Uyghur backness harmony (colloquium slides, CSU Fullerton). https://sites.socsci.uci.edu/~cjmayer/papers/cmayer_csuf_colloquium_may_2023.pdf
